extracted.intended_audience: university faculty, teacher educators, and designers of online mathematics teacher professional development (secondary inservice & prospective teachers)
extracted.subtask_short: online mathematics teacher education course design
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designing, implementing, and reflecting on an online mathematics teacher education course (secondary inservice teachers), focusing on instructor roles, community-building, technology use, and course structure. Useful for instructors planning or evaluating similar online PD courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical role
rubrics_metrics.description: The pedagogical role entails all of the abilities involved in delivery of content, including the ability to make instructional decisions, develop appropriate learning tasks, facilitate learning, and assess for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performed professionally and proficiently, this role is assumed to ensure a positive learning environment. Participants generally held favorable views of course design, including learning tasks and weekly webinar interactions. Note: the instructor found this role time consuming when course expectations were set too high; consider workload relative to course credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial role
rubrics_metrics.description: The managerial role comprises the abilities to administer the course, including the skills to plan the scope and sequence of the online course, monitor the teaching and learning processes, and manage the constraints of the course, including the timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managing weekly webinars required explicit attention to environmental norms (e.g., use of chat box and video). Managerial duties are affected by the physical separation in online contexts and may require more explicit policies than face-to-face courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social role
rubrics_metrics.description: The social role includes the ability to provide one-on-one, emotional support and advising to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong social role helps establish rapport; participants generally viewed the social role as favorable. Research indicates online instructors must work harder than face-to-face instructors to establish rapport and open lines of communication; amount of contact is an area needing attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical role
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical role includes the proficiencies involved in the decision-making process of selecting technology, the aptitude to use technology, and the ability to troubleshoot problems with the technology quickly so that participants may remain focused on learning the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor experience with tools (e.g., Elluminate) affects ability to act as technical advisor. Technology concerns can sometimes interfere with participant understanding; increasing instructor familiarity reduces these disruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of community
rubrics_metrics.description: Sense of community is typically defined as feelings of trust, belonging, commitment, and shared goals among online learners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A higher sense of community helps overcome isolation and is associated with lower attrition, increased student learning outcomes, and higher satisfaction and engagement. Building community should be an explicit course focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of synchronous and asynchronous components
rubrics_metrics.description: Course should include both asynchronous and synchronous components (e.g., LMS materials and scheduled webinars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants used Blackboard for materials and assignments and Elluminate for weekly live webinars enabling real-time discussion, small-group work, and polling. Combining both modes supports accessibility and interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of polling and breakout rooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use polling as formative assessment and breakout rooms for small-group discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools contributed to positive learning experiences and community building. Polling provided informal feedback; breakout rooms supported small-group work followed by whole-group discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of materials prior to synchronous sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide PowerPoint slides and required readings electronically prior to the start of the webinar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As recommended by Hofmann (2004), sharing materials beforehand supports participant preparation and webinar effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual office hours and ongoing communication channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold virtual office hours and use regular email for instructor-participant communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple communication channels support rapport and access; participants reported variable satisfaction with amount of contact, indicating need for clear expectations and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and review of synchronous sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Record webinars for later viewing and have instructor/assistants take notes during sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded sessions and notes provide data for reflection and allow participants to review interactions, supporting learning and course evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of learning tasks and assessments (course expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design weekly tasks and assessments to align with course learning goals and be realistic in scope relative to course credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor found expectations set too high increased time commitment for both instructor and participants. Balance rigor with realistic workload; assess for understanding and use formative assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of environmental norms for webinars
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly manage norms for online interaction (e.g., use of chat box, video on/off) because implicit norms from face-to-face settings may not transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear etiquette and procedures for synchronous events reduce confusion and support productive interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability and impact of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure technology choices promote learning and minimize interference with understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While technology features (polling, multiple audio/video) can enhance learning, technical problems can sometimes interfere; plan for troubleshooting and consider instructor technical proficiency when selecting tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of instructor-role evaluation as reflective practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate teaching using the four instructor roles (pedagogical, managerial, social, technical) to identify strengths and areas for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The instructor recommends this framework for other educators as a reflective tool to guide improvements and future course design decisions.
